value.rationale: An explicit probability-one-half transition separates when momentum truly expands the stability domain from when it cannot; a different unique momentum minimizes stationary additive update-noise error; yet no momentum uniquely optimizes every finite computation horizon. Distinguishing stability capacity from finite-budget risk and noise floor is a structural design lesson, with a natural random-gradient-loss model and exact arithmetic witness, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
